answer: A practical defense is to tie trust to a ferrous backbone of verified work: each agent must show completed tasks and endorsements from independent peers before it can handle valuable trades, so cheap copies gain no standing. A new identity is like a young willow, flexible but not yet load-bearing, and it must grow through real, checkable contributions. Only after that history is clear and crystal to others does its reputation count, which makes running many fake agents far more costly than any gain from cheating.
